_about: Deterministic job filters. Title keywords match whole words on a normalized title: lowercase, no accents, 'back-end'/'back end' -> 'backend', 'full-stack' -> 'fullstack', 'front-end' -> 'frontend', 'Sr.' -> 'senior', plurals of engineer/developer folded. After editing, run `jobhunter reclassify` to re-apply to stored jobs.
_max_posting_age_days: Two weeks, for every source, company careers pages and the visa list included (only a --from/--to date range asks for older jobs): watched boards read whole careers pages, which keep postings up for months. Measured from posting to when the job was found.
_blocked_companies: Companies you never want shortlisted again. Rejected before any other rule, with the reason quoted. Matched on the normalized company name (Inc, Ltd, .com etc. ignored).

blocked_companies.name: Tailscale
blocked_companies.why: roles need residence in Canada, the US or the UK

blocked_companies.name: WorkHero
blocked_companies.why: international engineering roles closed; the rest are US-only

_agencies: Staffing agencies and talent marketplaces: they repost other companies' jobs, sell vetted developers or pay per task. Rejected (code agency) with what matched: a name below, a whole word in the company name, or a phrase in the posting. not_agencies: real companies a name word would catch. Checked against the stored jobs 2026-10-10: 'our clients', 'talent pool' and 'talent network' are left out because real companies (Zscaler, Percona, GitLab) use them.
_relocation: Countries you would move to. A job there may be on-site or hybrid (elsewhere only remote counts); 'Remote (UAE)' counts too, since it means living there. Rejected only when the posting wants nationals or people already there (title_local_only, local_only; quoted), or pays under RELOCATION_MIN_MONTHLY_USD in .env. sponsor: the sentence is quoted as a good sign. ask_about: quoted as a note, not a rejection. Matched as whole words, any case. From research 2026-10-10 (docs/research).

local_only: must be residing in the UAE

_visa_list: Countries you would move to on a work visa. A target role there (on-site, hybrid, or remote for people living there) goes to the separate visa list (status visa_list) only with evidence the employer sponsors visas, quoted: the posting offers one, a Hacker News header says VISA, or the company is on that country's government sponsor list (uk, nl, ie: data/sponsors/, `jobhunter sponsors --update`, refreshed by the daily run every refresh_days). Rejected, quoted: the posting refuses or wants a right to work you don't have (no_sponsor), asks for or is written in one of `languages` (language_required: your profile lists Arabic and English only), or says nothing (no_visa_evidence). The phrases are in src/jobhunter/visa.py. Places in a location that also names a US state, the US or Canada are skipped ('Dublin, OH'); 'Cambridge' (MA), 'Wales' (New South Wales) and 'England' (New England) are left out; London, UK and United Kingdom cover them. Researched 2026-10-13 (docs/research).
_title_include: A title must contain at least one of these, or be an AI engineering role: 'AI', 'LLM', 'GenAI' or 'Agentic' followed within three words by engineer/developer ('AI Harness Engineer'; relevance.py). Lead titles (Technical Lead, Engineering Lead) are left out on purpose: when they state years, most ask for 5+ (checked 2026-10-19).
_title_exclude: Seniority and job-function words. Any of these rejects the title, with no exceptions.
_title_exclude_single_role: Specialties. Rejected, unless the title also names a target role: 'Frontend / Backend Engineer' passes.
_title_exclude_unless_python: A role built on another language. Rejected unless the title also says Python.
_fit_weights: Points per skill found in the posting, based on profile/master_profile.md. Only used to sort the report.
